cards.claim: The noise scale (β = ηB/N) determines convergence and generalization behavior; learning rate decay and batch size increase are equivalent when noise scale is held constant.
cards.conditions: SGD and variants (momentum, Nesterov, Adam) on CIFAR-10 and ImageNet; constant learning rate throughout training
cards.effect: Training and test curves remain nearly identical across schedules that maintain equivalent noise scale, despite 2.7× reduction in parameter updates
cards.evidence: Empirical results on Wide ResNet CIFAR-10 and Inception-ResNet-V2 ImageNet showing three training schedules (decaying LR, increasing BS, hybrid) produce indistinguishable learning curves
cards.quote: the noise scale which should decay, all three schedules should be indistinguishable

cards.claim: An optimal batch size exists that maximizes test set accuracy at constant learning rate, arising when noise scale is optimal, with scaling relationship B ∝ η.
cards.conditions: Multiple optimizers and datasets (CIFAR-10, ImageNet); batch size in range below training set size (B/N << 1)
cards.effect: Test accuracy peaks at specific batch size; deviations either direction reduce generalization
cards.evidence: Literature review citing Smith & Le (2017) and empirical validation across CIFAR-10 and ImageNet experiments showing generalization gap
cards.quote: Smith & Le (2017) observed an optimal batch size which maximized the test set accuracy at constant learning rate... this optimal batch size arises when the noise scale is also optimal

cards.claim: Linear scaling rule: learning rate can be increased proportionally with batch size (η ∝ B) while preserving test accuracy and convergence epochs.
cards.conditions: SGD with momentum, when B/N << 1; CIFAR-10 and ImageNet; batch sizes up to 8192 for ImageNet
cards.effect: ResNet-50 on ImageNet trained to 76.3% accuracy with 8192-image batches and proportionally scaled learning rate; parameter updates reduced by ~40% while maintaining epochs
cards.evidence: Empirical result from Goyal et al. (2017); replicated in this work with ResNet-50 on TPU achieving 76.1% in 30 minutes
cards.quote: Goyal et al. (2017) exploited a linear scaling rule between batch size and learning rate to train ResNet-50 on ImageNet in one hour with batches of 8192 images

cards.claim: Increasing momentum coefficient above 0.9 while scaling batch size to maintain noise scale reduces final test accuracy.
cards.conditions: SGD with momentum on CIFAR-10 (Wide ResNet); momentum varied from 0.9 to 0.98; initial LR = 0.5, max batch size = 6400
cards.effect: Test accuracy drops from 94.3% (m=0.9) to 93.3% (m=0.98) despite reducing parameter updates to <2500 and maintaining noise scale
cards.evidence: Direct experimental comparison of four schedules with identical noise scale decay but different momentum coefficients
cards.quote: Finally 'Increased momentum coefficient' requires less than 2500 parameter updates, but reaches a lower test accuracy of 93.3

cards.claim: The accumulation variable in momentum has initialization timescale ~1/(1-m) epochs; when this timescale becomes several epochs long, accumulation cannot adapt to loss landscape changes.
cards.conditions: SGD with momentum at training start; high momentum coefficients; epochs comparable to or shorter than accumulation timescale
cards.effect: Parameter update rates are suppressed during accumulation growth phase, reducing effective convergence rate; large momentum makes accumulation inflexible to loss changes
cards.evidence: Theoretical analysis in Section 4 with supporting observation from ImageNet experiments where larger momentum requires more parameter updates to reach accuracy plateau
cards.quote: We find that the accumulation grows in exponentially towards its steady state value over a 'timescale' of approximately training epochs... Once this timescale becomes several epochs long, the accumulation cannot adapt to changes in the loss landscape, impeding training

cards.claim: The linear scaling rule (B/η ∝ const) breaks down and must be abandoned when batch size approaches training set size (B/N → 1); learning rate decay must then be used for further noise scale reduction.
cards.conditions: Batch size reaching saturation near training set size; CIFAR-10 (50k images, max batch 6400) and ImageNet (1.28M images, max batch 65536)
cards.effect: Noise scale reduction cannot proceed via batch size increase beyond this threshold; transition to learning rate decay becomes necessary
cards.evidence: Explicit constraint applied in ImageNet experiments with maximum batch sizes set; ImageNet-2500 experiment uses batch-size saturation followed by LR decay at epochs 30, 60, 80
cards.quote: there are 50000 images in the CIFAR-10 training set... we decided to set a maximum batch size

cards.claim: Small batch training generalizes better than large batch training when the same noise scale trajectory is maintained; equivalence holds for test accuracy when noise scale (not LR) is controlled.
cards.conditions: CIFAR-10 and ImageNet with multiple architectures; comparing schedules with constant vs. increasing batch size but equivalent noise decay
cards.effect: No accuracy penalty for large-batch schedules if noise scale path is preserved; generalization gap arises only when noise scale is mismanaged
cards.evidence: Figure 3-4 results show test accuracies of three schedules (small batch with LR decay, large batch with constant LR, hybrid) overlap within variance; Keskar et al. claim confirmed in batch-size-increase context
cards.quote: it is now increasingly accepted that small batch training often generalizes better to the test set than large batch training

cards.claim: The equivalence between learning rate decay and batch size increase (noise scale control) holds across optimizer family including SGD, SGD with momentum, Nesterov momentum, and Adam.
cards.conditions: Wide ResNet on CIFAR-10; three schedules (decaying LR, constant LR with batch increase, hybrid); momentum = 0.9 for momentum methods; default Adam parameters
cards.effect: All optimizers show near-identical test accuracy curves and parameter update counts across the three schedules; Figure 3-4 curves overlap within noise
cards.evidence: Parallel experiments on same architecture and dataset, three optimizer classes, showing consistency of noise-scale principle
cards.quote: This procedure is successful for stochastic gradient descent (SGD), SGD with momentum, Nesterov momentum, and Adam. It reaches equivalent test accuracies after the same number of training epochs, but with fewer parameter updates

cards.claim: Batch size increase alone (without learning rate increase) reduces parameter update count by ~2.7× to 3.6× while preserving test accuracy per epoch.
cards.conditions: Wide ResNet on CIFAR-10; replacing LR decay schedule with equivalent batch size increase; momentum = 0.9
cards.effect: Parameter updates drop from 80,000 (LR decay) to ~29,000 (BS increase) while final test accuracy stays 94.3%–94.4%
cards.evidence: Direct comparison in Figures 2–3 showing 'Increasing batch size' schedule achieves identical accuracy curve to 'Decaying learning rate' baseline
cards.quote: all three schedules match up to the first 'step', after this point increasing the batch size dramatically reduces the number of parameter updates required to train the model
